priceSnapshot.note: changePct is +0.16% against OKX open24h of 63,063.7. Against the PRIOR REPORT - today's morning session at 63,060.5 - the move is +104.6 points, +0.17%, over four hours and twenty-seven minutes. That is the largest inter-session move in six sessions and it is the first one this desk has recorded to the UPSIDE since 13 August. The path matters more than the endpoint: the 16:00Z hour opened 63,146.7 and ran to 63,390.0 on 236.4 BTC of volume - eight times the hourly average of the preceding five bars - then settled 63,255.1, and the live 17:00Z bar has given back to 63,165.1. So the session made a decisive break, fired the morning's add gate on a settled close, and has since returned 224.9 points below its high. The run proxy served this endpoint from a stale cache again this session; every OKX number in this report was re-read in-browser from the okx.com origin with a live timestamp inside three minutes of publication.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $63,056.4 - this session's low, printed on the 14:00Z bar. The line moves UP 92.1 points from morning's 62,964.3, which was tested this morning and never revisited. That is the first time in six sessions this desk has been able to raise the reduce level rather than lower it, and it is the mechanical consequence of a session that never traded below its opening hour. What a break of 63,056.4 would mean is specific: it would put price back under the 1H ema50 at 63,113.8 and under the whole 15m EMA stack that was reclaimed at 15:00Z, and it would say the 63,390 push was pure short-covering with nothing behind it. The level also sits 21.4 points above the 63,035 long-liquidation cluster, so a settled close below it hands price straight to the only unburned fuel on the map.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $63,390.0 - this session's high. The rule introduced by the morning report, anchoring the add gate to the session high rather than republishing a stale number, worked on its first outing: morning set 63,155.8 and the 16:00Z bar settled 63,255.1, a clean settled close above it, after trading to 63,390.0. The gate fired, so it moves up to the new session high. A settled close above 63,390.0 would be materially different from today's spike, because the spike came with FALLING open interest - $2,115,031,058 now against $2,133,716,637 at the morning read, down 0.88% - which is the signature of shorts covering rather than longs building. An add that arrives with open interest rising through 63,390 is the confirmation this tape has not produced once this week.

decisionBox.changed: Both ends of the box move UP, which has not happened since 13 August. The reduce level rises 92.1 points to 63,056.4 to track the new session low; the add gate rises 234.2 points to 63,390.0 because morning's 63,155.8 FIRED on a settled 1H close at 63,255.1. Invalidation tightens 118.0 points from 62,846.3 to 62,964.3, today's low and the level midnight and morning independently derived - with a higher session low in place, an invalidation 210 points below the reduce line was measuring nothing. The position stays ADD, and unlike morning this ADD is executing a trigger the desk published four hours ago rather than anticipating one. The honest counterweight is in the addIf text: the break that fired the gate ran on shrinking leverage, not growing it.

liquidations.note: All read in-browser from the okx.com origin; the run proxy was again serving these endpoints from a stale cache and those values were discarded. THE HEADLINE IS THE DIVERGENCE BETWEEN PRICE AND LEVERAGE. Open interest is $2,115,031,058 at 17:50:04Z against $2,133,716,637 at the morning read - DOWN $18,685,580 or 0.88% - while price rose 104.6 points and printed a 333.6-point range. Open interest falling into a rally is short-covering, not accumulation, and it reverses morning's finding that leverage had turned up after five declines. The liquidation ledger says the same thing from the other side: $182,330 short-side against $123,371 long-side over the last 21 hours, where the same feed read 3.5-to-1 LONG this morning, because $148,367 of short-side fuel was consumed between 16:16Z and 16:34Z. Funding is the one input pointing the other way - the current period reads +0.00519% into the 00:00Z settlement against the +0.00972% unsettled figure morning saw, so the carry cost has HALVED even as price rose, which means longs are not paying up to chase this. The account ratio is 2.22 against morning's 2.23: retail did not de-risk into the rally and did not add to it either. Net read - the move up was shorts being forced out of a crowded-long tape, and nobody with size has stepped in behind them yet.

calibration.note: The prior report is today's 2026-08-16-morning, published at 08:30:00-05:00 with spot at 63,060.5. Its reduce line at 62,964.3 did NOT fire: the session low since publication is 63,056.4, 92.1 points above it, and no 1H bar came close. Its add gate at 63,155.8 DID fire, and it fired properly - the 16:00Z bar traded to 63,390.0 and SETTLED at 63,255.1, a clean settled close 99.3 points above the gate, exactly the confirmation the morning report specified. That matters beyond one trade. Morning broke with midnight to move the add gate down from a level republished seven consecutive times without a single test, on the argument that a gate price never approaches is decoration. The relocated gate was tested and taken within four and a half hours. The rule is now evidenced, not just argued, and this report applies it again by moving the gate to the new session high of 63,390.0. actingHelped is rated TRUE on the position rather than on the trigger, and the distinction is worth recording. The wallet's morning tranche went on at 63,060.5 and is now +104.6 points, +0.17%. A trader who instead waited and bought the 63,155.8 gate itself is at 63,165.1, up 9.3 points - essentially flat. So the ADD stance helped and the ADD trigger did not, which is the same lesson midnight and morning argued about from the other direction yesterday: a level judged on settled bars and a level judged at the mark give different answers, and the wallet only ever experiences the mark. The one finding this session must set against its own bullish read is that the rally ran on FALLING open interest, down 0.88% to $2,115,031,058, so the move that fired the gate was shorts being closed out rather than buyers arriving.
